mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investments, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months indicates a strengthening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of the instances when the housing starts are increasing.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points within two months signals an improving labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) over three consecutive months indicates a robust supply-side activity, which is a strong signal of economic expansion and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of the instances when industrial production is increasing.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow faster than GDP (GDPC1) over a quarter, it signals a consumption-driven economic expansion, which is likely to lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > GDPC1 growth in 1 quarter
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 1% within a month signals inflationary pressures, which typically leads to monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) show a decline for two consecutive months, it signals a weakening labor market, which is likely to lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year change in real GDP (GDPC1) is negative, it indicates an economic contraction, which is likely to lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of the instances when the GDP is contracting.
